title: Western Michigan University unveils Valley Oaks residence hall for students
text:
Western Michigan University unveils Valley Oaks residence hall for students
C. M. Cullen
Western Michigan University celebrated the opening of its newest residence hall, Valley Oaks, during a ribbon-cutting ceremony on July 29 in Kalamazoo, Mich.
Dr. Diane Anderson, vice president for student affairs, said, “We really tried to think of everything to meet students where they are, foster belonging and help them thrive here at Western, and the result is even better than I could have imagined. I can’t wait for our students and families to see it.”
Valley Oaks spans 274,000 square feet across four stories and is recognized as the largest mass timber project in Michigan. The building incorporates biophilic design elements intended to integrate the natural wooded landscape with interior living spaces. Dr. Barry Olson, associate vice president for student affairs, said, “This project is an entirely different approach to a residence hall at Western; it’s really a game changer for us. When you walk in, the first thing you notice is the smell of wood. You see all these beautiful columns and exposed timber and large windows that let in natural light; it just feels very much like you’re bringing the outside in. There’s a really grounding and calming presence.” Janice Quakenbush, director of finance and infrastructure for student affairs, added that mass timber supports sustainability efforts by reducing the carbon footprint compared to traditional construction methods.
The facility will house approximately 1,000 first-year students with pod-style housing options including single rooms and single-occupancy bathrooms. Common areas include kitchenettes on each floor as well as a larger community kitchen on the main floor; laundry rooms; air conditioning units in each room; collaboration hubs; wellness amenities such as a massage chair; outdoor decks; fire pits; privacy booths for phone calls or telehealth appointments; two distinct courtyards designed for relaxation or recreation; and accessible routes throughout.
Roshona Porter, director of housing and residence life, said programming spaces were designed based on community input: “Students told us they wanted spaces that allowed them to connect and build community so we made that a priority.” She also said: “Valley Oaks is intentionally designed with multiple lounges and collaboration spaces that offer open inviting areas for students to come together.”
Quakenbush said she hopes families feel reassured when seeing Valley Oaks: “Families should feel reassured and confident that their student is entering a safe space that promotes belonging so their students can focus on their academic success and well-being.” Porter concluded, “Valley Oaks is a physical embodiment of the Office of Housing and Residence Life’s values in action: spaces that support student well-being, spark relationships, reflect our commitment to equity, and support student growth for years to come... It’s a model for how we want to continue designing residential life at WMU: intentionally, collaboratively and with our values built into every corner of the space.”
Western Michigan University fields 16 Division I varsity sports as part of its Mid-American Conference membership while enrolling more than 17,000 students, according to the official website. The university emphasizes learner-focused education supported by research initiatives, promotes sustainability through LEED-certified buildings, and maintains top-100 national rankings among graduate programs. It also supports inclusive excellence campus-wide according to the official website.
